claim: Keys and signatures that identify a graphic or figure entry can collide, match rows in a different order, or move; mix in position and size, and do not key a sprite to an entry address.

evidence.text: Three 8-bit keys (sum, sum of sums, rotate and XOR) gave two striped poles the same keys; a sum plus a 16-bit hash with the size has no clash in 1,239 shapes.
A sum-based signature matched rows in another order; the cache signature is now order-sensitive.
A sprite table entry with no rows can hold the same address as a real one; a lookup by address must skip it.
Keying a sprite to a figure entry's address fails when the game swaps entries to sort them: one figure vanished and another doubled for a frame; the flicker tool found it.
